name: Lord Windgrace
description: A panther warrior planeswalker and one of Urza's Nine Titans who despises the destructive power of artifice and bound his soul to Urborg.

description_citations.text: "Windgrace". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: When Urza activates the Golgothian Sylex, Urborg becomes partially submerged and turns into a swamp; Windgrace is born.
timeline.quote: the jungle island of Urborg became partially submerged and turned into a swamp

citation.text: "Urborg", section "Aftermath of the Sylex Blast". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Ravidel visits Urborg to recruit Lord Windgrace, who rejects him; Ravidel takes a shard of Urborgan obsidian.
timeline.quote: Before departing, Ravidel took a shard of Urborgan obsidian with him

citation.text: "Planeswalker War", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Ravidel visits Urborg and fails to convince Lord Windgrace, an isolationist, to join him; he takes a chunk of obsidian.
timeline.quote: Ravidel leaves, not able to convince the panther warrior .

citation.text: "Prelude to War", section "Journeying Angel , by Art Holcomb". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Legacy Weapon saves Dominaria and seemingly destroys Yawgmoth; only Freyalise and Windgrace of the Nine survive.
timeline.quote: Freyalise, along with all of Dominaria, was saved by the activation of the Legacy Weapon, which seemingly destroyed Yawgmoth.

citation.text: "Freyalise", section "Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lord Windgrace performs the ritual of Dalfir on Taysir's body.
timeline.quote: performed the ritual of Dalfir on him

citation.text: "Taysir of Rabiah", section "Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Windgrace closes the time rift above the Stronghold ruins at the cost of his life.
timeline.quote: The time rift was closed by Lord Windgrace at the expense of his life.

citation.text: "Urborg", section "First Phyrexian invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Bo Levar, Guff, Freyalise and Windgrace discover Urza's treachery and Taysir's death and decide to set off the Soul Bombs manually.
timeline.quote: They decide to set off the Soul Bombs manually.

citation.text: "Apocalypse (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The cloud kills the minotaur and metathran armies on Urborg except a small group saved by Lord Windgrace.
timeline.quote: brought to Hurloon by Lord Windgrace just in time

citation.text: "Apocalypse (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Teferi, Jhoira and Venser go to an alternate Urborg timeline and help Venser planeswalk home.
timeline.quote: Teferi and Jhoira used their magic to help Venser complete his first planeswalk

citation.text: "Jhoira", section "Fighting the Phyrexians". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lord Windgrace gives up his life to heal the Urborg rift.
timeline.quote: he gave up his life to heal the rift

citation.text: "Rift", section "Urborg rift". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Windgrace returns home and sets rules limiting technology, deputizing the Windgrace Acolytes.
timeline.quote: He deputized several human and panther warriors as the Windgrace Acolytes

citation.text: "Urborg", section "Windgrace's rule". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Windgrace sacrifices his spark and life, fusing his spirit to Urborg to watch over it.
timeline.quote: he performed a spell to fuse his spirit to Urborg and watch over it

citation.text: "Urborg", section "Windgrace's rule". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Windgrace sacrifices himself to seal the rift over the Stronghold.
timeline.quote: Windgrace sacrificed himself to seal the rift over the Stronghold in Urborg

citation.text: "Dominaria (plane)", section "Rift Era". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Legendary planeswalkers sacrifice their sparks or lives to close the rifts.
timeline.quote: to sacrifice their sparks or lives to close the rifts

citation.text: "Rift Era", section "The Temporal Crisis". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Weaver King takes control of slivers to wage war on their former masters.
timeline.quote: Once the Weaver King discovered the simplicity of their hivemind, he quickly took control of them for his purposes and used them to wage war on their former masters.

citation.text: "Sliver", section "After the apocalypse". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lord Windgrace gives his life to close the rift above the Stronghold, lingering as a guardian spirit.
timeline.quote: gave his life to close the rift above the Stronghold

citation.text: "Temporal Crisis of Dominaria", section "Resolution". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Venser lives alone in a workshop in the Urborg swamps, salvaging Phyrexian remains and building his Ambulator while drawing Windgrace's ire.
timeline.quote: he lived alone in a workshop within the Urborg swamps, salvaging parts from the remains of Phyrexians left from the Invasion

citation.text: "Venser", section "Life in Urborg". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Windgrace catches Venser, who becomes one of his gladehunters.
timeline.quote: Venser agreed to become one of Windgrace's gladehunters, taking the planeswalker's mark upon his skin

citation.text: "Venser", section "The Mending". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Jhoira and Venser go to Urborg to seek Lord Windgrace; Venser is captured by Windgrace and Jhoira meets Jodah, who explains the Weaver King.
timeline.quote: Venser is captured by Lord Windgrace while Jhoira encounters Jodah

citation.text: "Planar Chaos (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Windgrace consults Teferi, who deduces the Phyrexians come from an alternate reality; Windgrace takes the group to the Blind Eternities to meet Freyalise, and they decide to pursue the rifts independently.
timeline.quote: Windgrace and Freyalise decide to pursue each rift independently.

citation.text: "Planar Chaos (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn arrives and convinces Windgrace to close the Urborg rift; Windgrace crushes the rift but fades from reality, apparently dead.
timeline.quote: he fades from reality as well, apparently dead.

citation.text: "Planar Chaos (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: During Sheoldred's invasion, Windgrace's Soul rises from the land to defend it.
timeline.quote: Windgrace's Soul rose from the land to defend it against the invaders

citation.text: "Urborg", section "Second Phyrexian Invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Windgrace sacrifices his life to protect Urborg, first binding his soul to the land and vowing to watch over it.
timeline.quote: He sacrificed his life to protect his home of Urborg, but not before binding his soul to the land and vowing to always watch over it.

citation.text: "Windgrace". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

relations.note: Nantuko in Urborg are said to serve Lord Windgrace in the Time Spiral novel.
relations.quote: In the Time Spiral novel , there are mentions of Nantukos still living in Urborg, and serving Lord Windgrace .

citation.text: "Insect", section "Urborg". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.
